heading: INT. ABANDONED RADIO STATION - STUDIO B - NIGHT

units.text: INT. ABANDONED RADIO STATION - STUDIO B - NIGHT
A dead studio.
Foam panels hanging in strips.
A broadcast desk dusted with plaster.
A single red ON AIR bulb, unlit.
Cold breath hangs in the beam of a flashlight.
A WOMAN in a drenched raincoat limps through the door, flashlight gripped in both hands, the beam shaking over the room.
Mud to the knees.
A cut at her hairline.
She shuts the door behind her, drags the desk's heavy chair in front of it, and wedges the back under the knob.
Her breathing is loud in the dead air.
She sweeps the beam across the booth.
Dials.
Faders.
A coffee mug with the mold of years.
A corkboard of staff photos and a laminated badge hanging from a nail on a lanyard.
Okay. Okay. Okay.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: She crosses to the desk, plants the flashlight on its end so the beam strikes the ceiling, and shrugs off her coat.
She flips the toggle on the console.
Nothing.
She flips it again.
A hum, then a tick, and the ON AIR bulb glows red, flooding the booth in a color like a wound.
She jumps back, knocking the mug onto the floor.
It shatters.
She waits.
Nothing answers.
She crouches, picks up the lanyard, and reads the badge in the red light, turning it toward the beam.
Nell Okonjo-Reyes. Overnight host.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: She looks at the photograph on the badge.
It looks like her.
She lifts a hand to her own face, pressing the cut, then drops it.
That's me.
units.name: NELL

units.text: A hiss from the speaker above the desk.
Then a voice, her own, thin and recorded, slowed by the failing tape.
...if you're hearing this, Nell, don't go to the lobby. Don't open the second door. Whatever it says in your voice, it isn't you.
units.name: NELL

units.text: Nell stares at the speaker.
The tape runs on in hiss.
Behind her, in the corridor, something slides along the wall, patient, in no hurry.
The chair against the door creaks as its back leg shifts a quarter-inch.
She does not turn.
She takes the badge, wraps the lanyard once around her wrist, grabs the flashlight, and with a trembling hand switches off the red light.
The booth goes black.
Stay in the dark. It can't read what it can't see.
units.name: NELL

units.text: In the dark, a soft knock comes at the door.
Once.
Twice.
Then a voice, calm and warm, her own.
Nell? It's me. Let me in.
units.name: NELL

units.text: Nell stands rigid in the black.
Her lips move.
She says nothing.
The knocking stops.
The chair creaks again, steadily, as though a patient hand is pressing from the other side.
No.
units.name: NELL
